pr_title: Try other resolved IPs if one fails to connect
pr_body:
When `HTTPClient` and `WebSocketClient` are connecting to server, save all resolved IPs, and try other candidates if one failed to connect. Not [Happy Eyeballs](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc8305), but at least it's happy I think :)

Fixes #46972, and hopefully fixes #36418, I don't have IPv6 connection to the AssetLib, so I only tested on my `localhost` which resolved to IPv6 first.

It's the same for 3.x, but `core/io/http_client_tcp.{h,cpp}` → `core/io/http_client.{h,cpp}` and `container.is_empty()` → `container.empty()`.
pr_comments:
~Cherry-picked for 3.3.4.~

*Edit:* Undid cherry-pick, it requires `resolve_hostname_addresses` which doesn't exist in `3.3`.

issue_context.title: Godot editor build doesn't connect to WebSocket server (client in HTML5 works)
issue_context.body:
**Godot version:**
3.2.3 stable

**OS/device including version:**
Windows GLES2

**Issue description:**
When I run godot project via editor it doesnt do anything related to websocket but when I export it to HTML5 and run it then same code can connect to websocket. What might the reason be?
PS: I am trying everything in same PC


**Steps to reproduce:**
Start a websocket server, code websocket client on godot, run in editor it does nothing
comments:
@berk-can Please upload a [minimal reproduction project](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#provide-a-simple-example-project) to make this easier to troubleshoot.

Also, which program are you using to host the WebSocket server?

Likely the usual dual stack IPv4/IPv6 issue and `localhost` being resolved as `::1` while the server listens on `127.0.0.1`.
See #45249 and https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/36418#issuecomment-589963787 .

review_comments: `ip_candidates` should also be cleared when reaching `STATUS_CONNECTED` (i.e. fully connected, including SSL handshake).
